assessment.nobel_worthiness: Active-matter hydrodynamics is a clean example of what I look for: a simple, universal mechanism (self-propelled units with alignment) that produces long-range order in two dimensions in apparent defiance of the Mermin-Wagner argument, and generic giant number fluctuations and anomalous scaling. The Vicsek model gave the minimal numerical model, Toner and Tu gave the continuum theory and renormalization-group exponents, and Ramaswamy and collaborators established the symmetry-based hydrodynamics of orientationally ordered active fluids. It spans flocks, bacterial suspensions and cytoskeletal assays and has reshaped non-equilibrium statistical physics.
assessment.attribution: The Vicsek model (1995), Toner-Tu (1995, 1998) and the Ramaswamy-Simha-Toner line of work are the identifiable foundations. The three credited names form a natural, intellectually distinct trio of numerics, field theory and hydrodynamics. Yuhai Tu and Aditi Simha are significant co-authors who are not in the supplied credit list, so the three-person cap leaves some credit unresolved. I cannot add them.
assessment.maturity: Quantitative confirmation is good for giant number fluctuations (vibrated granular layers, bacterial and colloidal systems), but the exact exponents of the flocking phase are only partially tested experimentally, and the Toner-Tu exponents are known mostly from one-loop and numerical analysis. The field is mature enough for the core ideas and still growing quickly, so recognition would be timely rather than premature.
uncertainties: Experimental tests of the precise Toner-Tu scaling exponents remain limited and are debated.
Allocation among Vicsek, Toner, Tu, Ramaswamy and Simha is not clean and I have not verified the details of priority.
Whether the committee sees this as physics proper or as an interdisciplinary application is a possible concern.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction of the quantum spin Hall effect and the Z2 topological insulator is a conceptually deep and economical result: a topological invariant protects conducting edge and surface states in a time-reversal-invariant band insulator. It opened a large field of topological band theory with real materials, and the experimental realization in HgTe quantum wells gave the decisive confirmation. The mechanism is simple and general, and it extends the topological-phase ideas recognised in 2016.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele (2005) introduced the Z2 classification and the graphene-based quantum spin Hall model, and Molenkamp's group did the HgTe experiment following the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal. Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang are not in the credited names, and Zhang's death complicates the picture. Within the supplied names the Kane, Mele, Molenkamp trio is a defensible and fair configuration, though it is not the only reasonable one. Moore, Balents, Fu and Roy (three-dimensional case) are also not credited.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed independently in many materials (HgTe, Bi-Sb, Bi2Se3 via ARPES), with well-understood theory. Very mature and sufficiently long after the 2005-2008 discoveries, so timely and arguably overdue.
uncertainties: The proposal by Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang and the three-dimensional work by Fu, Kane, Mele and Moore make priority contested.
The precise form of the credit for the theory versus the experiment is open.
Practical device impact is still limited.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Fluctuation theorems are exact, model-independent relations for entropy production far from equilibrium, and they link the second law, time-reversal symmetry and microscopic reversibility. The Jarzynski equality turns non-equilibrium work into equilibrium free-energy differences. The idea is simple, general and rigorous, and it is the type of result I trust. It also connects with stochastic thermodynamics from colloids to single molecules.
assessment.attribution: The Evans-Cohen-Morriss (1993) work, the Gallavotti-Cohen theorem (1995) and the Jarzynski equality (1997) are the pillars. Crooks, Cohen, Searles and Kurchan are other major contributors who are not in the credit list, so the allocation is only partly clean. Within the supplied names I would give priority to the three.
assessment.maturity: Verified experimentally (optical tweezers pulling RNA hairpins, Bustamante and others; electronic and trapped-ion systems) and very well understood. Mature, with 25-30 years of confirmation.
uncertainties: The credit is spread over many people and the three-person cap is difficult to apply fairly.
The mathematical scope of the Gallavotti-Cohen theorem (chaotic hypothesis) is more restricted than the exact relations.
The committee may see it as more theoretical than discovery-driven.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The 1984 BPZ paper made conformal symmetry in two dimensions into an exactly solvable framework for critical phenomena and string worldsheets. It gives exact critical exponents for 2D statistical models, classifies universality classes, and underlies much of modern field theory and string theory. Few results better illustrate the unity of statistical physics and quantum field theory, which is a strong plus for me.
assessment.attribution: The decisive paper is Belavin, Polyakov and Zamolodchikov (1984), so all three credited names are natural laureates. Polyakov's prior contributions (conformal bootstrap ideas, 1970) and Friedan, Qiu and Shenker (unitarity) and Cardy are relevant but not credited. Zamolodchikov's death in 2023 would make the configuration impossible if the Nobel rules are applied strictly (no posthumous awards), which is a serious constraint I cannot verify here.
assessment.maturity: Theoretically enormous and long confirmed (Ising, Potts, tricritical models, quantum Hall edges, numerical bootstrap), but the Nobel Committee has rarely rewarded pure theory without a direct experimental discovery. Fully mature, perhaps unusually late.
uncertainties: Eligibility of a deceased candidate (I believe Zamolodchikov died in 2023, which I have not verified) may prevent this configuration.
Pure theory without a single experimental discovery has a high bar in physics.
Cardy and Friedan are not credited.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction of flat bands at magic twist angles by Bistritzer and MacDonald (2011) and the discovery of correlated insulators and superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene by Jarillo-Herrero's group (2018) opened moire physics as a tunable platform for strongly correlated phases. The scientific impact is high and the mechanism (an interference-controlled moire potential) is simple and elegant, with a clear connection between a clean theory and a clear experiment.
assessment.attribution: The theory-experiment pairing is natural: Bistritzer and MacDonald for the continuum model and magic angle, Jarillo-Herrero for the experiment. Cao and Fatemi (the experimental first authors) and other groups, e.g. Dean, Kim, Yazdani, are not in the credited names, and graphene-based work is closely linked to the 2010 prize. Three laureates are available inside the supplied names.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced across many groups and extended to moire TMDs, with many open questions about the pairing mechanism. The field is very active but its interpretation is not stable. It is probably early for me, although strong.
uncertainties: The superconducting mechanism and the nature of the correlated phases are not settled.
Experimental sample dependence and twist-angle disorder remain problems.
Contributions by earlier work (Lopes dos Santos, Peres and Castro Neto; Suarez Morell) may deserve mention.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Cirac and Zoller proposed the trapped-ion quantum gate (1995) and set up the theory of using cold atoms and ions for quantum computation and simulation. The ideas provide concrete physical routes from statistical-mechanics models to controllable quantum hardware, and they connect to my interest in computation and many-body physics. The impact on atomic and quantum-information physics is large.
assessment.attribution: The pair is a natural, compact configuration and each name is a decisive contributor. The prize in 2012 (Wineland and Haroche) and the 2022 prize (Aspect, Clauser, Zeilinger) already covered nearby experiments, so the overlap has to be weighed. Blatt and Wineland did the early experimental work and are not in this particular credit set.
assessment.maturity: Experimentally confirmed over three decades with trapped ions and Rydberg and lattice systems. Mature, and the interpretation is stable.
uncertainties: Overlap with previous Nobel prizes in quantum optics (2012, 2022) could lower the novelty.
The theory-only allocation sits awkwardly relative to the experimental groups.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Biomolecular condensates as liquid-liquid phase separated compartments in cells changed how we think about intracellular organization. The P-granule work is a physical statement: droplets with surface tension, wetting and dynamical arrest, treated with ideas from polymer and soft-matter physics. For a statistical physicist it is an attractive cross-disciplinary example, although the physics content is in part a reinterpretation of known phase-separation concepts.
assessment.attribution: Hyman and Brangwynne identified the liquid-like behavior of P granules (2009), and Jülicher contributed the theory of active droplets. Many others (Rosen, Rosen and Rosen, Pappu, Tanaka, Mittag) are not in the credit list, and the question of whether this is a physics or a chemistry/physiology prize is unresolved.
assessment.maturity: Well-replicated in vitro but under active debate in vivo about the functional role and the precise physical state (liquid, gel, or other). Interpretation is not fully stable, so recognition is likely premature for physics.
uncertainties: The in vivo relevance and the material state of condensates are debated.
Whether the committee would classify this as physics is uncertain.
Credit is diffuse among many groups.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The geometric phase is a simple and general mechanism for a phase acquired by cyclic adiabatic evolution, tied to curvature in parameter space. It unifies the Aharonov-Bohm effect, molecular Born-Oppenheimer physics, polarization optics and the Berry curvature that underlies the Hall conductivity and topological band theory. It is foundational for much of modern condensed matter and a good example of a result that was understood, not only observed.
assessment.attribution: Berry (1984) is the decisive paper, with Aharonov-Bohm (1959) and Aharonov-Anandan (1987) as strongly related. Pancharatnam (1956) and Longuet-Higgins and Mead-Truhlar anticipated aspects of it, which is exactly the type of priority question I would want examined. Simon (holonomy interpretation) and Anandan are not credited. Two named laureates is a clean configuration if Aharonov is deemed justified.
assessment.maturity: Extensively confirmed in optics, NMR, neutron and electron experiments, and by its consequences in solids. Very mature and arguably late. I note Berry is in his eighties.
uncertainties: Prior discoveries (Pancharatnam, Mead and Truhlar) leave credit unresolved.
Whether a prize should honour Aharonov for the geometric phase in addition to the Aharonov-Bohm effect is uncertain.
The work is conceptual and not a single decisive discovery.
